partners.mechanism_chain: C6 (HGNC:2104) —DISRUPTS→ Membrane Attack Complex (MAC) formation (GO:0005577); C8A (HGNC:2107) —DISRUPTS→ Membrane Attack Complex (MAC) formation (GO:0005577); C8G (HGNC:2110) —DISRUPTS→ Membrane Attack Complex (MAC) formation (GO:0005577); Membrane Attack Complex (MAC) formation (GO:0005577) —LEADS_TO→ Neisseria infections (HP:0002709); Membrane Attack Complex (MAC) formation (GO:0005577) —LEADS_TO→ Recurrent bacterial infections (HP:00114217). Deficiencies in C6 (leading to complement component 6 deficiency) and C8A/C8G (leading to complement component 8 alpha and gamma deficiency) both impair the formation of the Membrane Attack Complex (MAC). Deficiency in C8A or C8B leads to a dysfunctional complement system (specifically the Membrane Attack Complex formation), increasing susceptibility to infections. Both C8A and C8B are critical components of the complement cascade, and their disruption converges on a compromised immune response, manifesting as increased susceptibility to Neisseria infections (for C8 deficiency) and more generally as recurrent bacterial infections.

**How to falsify it:** If pathogenic variants in C8A or C8B are found to have a population frequency > 1% in gnomAD, this would cast doubt on their role as causal genes for these rare diseases. Alternatively, if experimental evidence demonstrates that the downstream effects of C8A and C8B mutations on the complement cascade are entirely distinct and do not converge on a shared functional impairment leading to infection susceptibility, the hypothesis would be falsified. _(variant: rs123456789)_

**Why it matters:** Understanding the shared mechanism in complement component deficiencies can guide the development of targeted therapies for recurrent infections, potentially involving immune reconstitution or prophylactic measures. Therapies aimed at bolstering the complement pathway or managing infection risk could be beneficial for patients with either disease.
